evidence: From the road end at Dawson Falls the Upper Mangōraukawa / Lake Dive Track follows Panitahi and Syme Hut Track through forest to the junction with the Lower Mangōraukawa / Lake Dive Track.
At the junction, the Mangōraukawa / Lake Dive Track heads left to follow marker poles across exposed alpine tussock slopes before descending steeply down to the lake.

evidence: From Dawson Falls Road end, the Lower Mangōraukawa / Lake Dive Track follows Panitahi and Syme Hut Track then branches left at the junction, passing Hastie’s Hill, undulating through forest and crossing many unbridged streams before arriving at the lake.

evidence: There are two options to get to Mangōraukawa / Lake Dive – the upper and lower tracks. You can combine the tracks to make a 13 km loop track.
It is better to return on the lower track during this time of year.

doubts: The page ('Lake Dive tracks') offers two tracks to the same lake and a loop combining them; kind network was chosen, with the upper track (listed first) as main, though the loop could equally be seen as the main walk. The tracks are given as one_way to the lake (DOC's 'one way' distances); the text does not say whether walkers return the same way, only that in winter it is better to return on the lower track. The loop's direction is not stated (W3 via order is up the upper track, back the lower track only as suggested for winter). Start ref is the Dawson Falls place (T3), next to the road end; none of the road-end features is named as the Panitahi and Syme Hut Track's start (F1 Hasties Hill Track is closest to T3). Hooker Shelter may not be a hut with bunks, so huts is empty. Whether Hastie's Hill turn off is the same as the lower track junction is unclear.
